# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Overview and Core Approach

The Labour Party's 2024 manifesto presents a plan centered on five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, expanding opportunity, and NHS reform. The document emphasizes fiscal responsibility, with commitments to balance day-to-day spending with revenues and reduce debt as a share of the economy.

## Economic Policy

Labour proposes establishing an Industrial Strategy Council to guide long-term economic planning across sectors including financial services, automotive, life sciences, and creative industries. A National Wealth Fund would receive £7.3 billion to invest in ports, gigafactories, steel, carbon capture, and green hydrogen production.

The party commits to capping corporation tax at 25%, maintaining full expensing for capital investment, and reforming business rates. Planning reform features prominently, with targets of 1.5 million new homes over the parliament, including restoration of mandatory housing targets and strategic greenbelt release.

Devolution would expand through new powers for combined authorities over transport, skills, housing, and employment support. Local Growth Plans would be developed with employers and educational institutions.

## Energy and Environment

The manifesto targets clean electricity by 2030 through doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind. Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, would receive £8.3 billion in capital.

Existing North Sea oil and gas licenses would continue, but no new exploration licenses would be issued. The windfall tax on energy companies would be extended and increased. A Warm Homes Plan would invest £6.6 billion to upgrade five million homes.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and establishing specialist rape units in every police force. The party commits to publishing independent workforce planning and delivering the long-term workforce plan.

Social care would move toward a National Care Service with national standards, including a Fair Pay Agreement for the sector.

## Crime and Justice

Neighbourhood policing would be restored through new recruitment funded by efficiency programs. Antisocial behaviour measures include new Respect Orders and specific offenses for assaults on retail workers. Knife crime initiatives include banning certain weapons, mandatory youth offending team referrals, and Young Futures hubs.

Violence against women and girls would be addressed through specialist police teams, fast-tracked rape cases, and domestic abuse experts in emergency call centers.

## Education and Skills

Education proposals include recruiting 6,500 teachers, establishing 3,000 primary school-based nurseries, and providing free breakfast clubs in all primary schools. Private school tax exemptions would end to fund state education.

Skills England would coordinate post-16 education, with the Apprenticeship Levy reformed into a Growth and Skills Levy. Further education colleges would become specialist Technical Excellence Colleges.

## Immigration and Borders

A Border Security Command would replace the Rwanda scheme, using counter-terrorism powers against smuggling networks. Additional caseworkers would address asylum backlogs, with a new returns unit to expedite removals. The Migration Advisory Committee would be strengthened to link immigration policy with skills development.

## Constitutional and Governance Reform

Hereditary peers would lose voting rights, and an 80-year retirement age would apply to the Lords. An Ethics and Integrity Commission would oversee ministerial standards. MPs would face bans on paid advisory roles.

Devolution relationships would be reset through a Council of Nations and Regions bringing together UK and devolved government leaders. Voting age would lower to 16.

## Foreign Policy and Defense

NATO commitment remains central, with a Strategic Defence Review planned. Military support for Ukraine would continue. The party commits to maintaining the nuclear deterrent and setting a path to 2.5% GDP defense spending.

EU relations would be improved through veterinary agreements, touring artist arrangements, and professional qualification recognition, while remaining outside the single market and customs union. A UK-EU security pact would be pursued.

## Funding

Revenue measures include abolishing non-dom tax status, closing private equity carried interest loopholes, extending energy windfall taxes, and ending private school VAT exemptions. Spending efficiencies target consultancy costs and asylum accommodation.
